edges.effect_quant: In the landmark adult trial, hydroxyurea lowered the median annual pain-crisis rate from 4.5 to 2.5 crises per year and reduced acute chest syndrome and transfusion use.
edges.population: children and adults with sickle cell disease, especially HbSS or HbSbeta0 thalassemia
edges.mechanism: Hydroxyurea raises fetal hemoglobin and reduces leukocyte-driven inflammation, making sickling less frequent and vaso-occlusion less severe. That translates into fewer painful crises, less acute chest syndrome, fewer hospitalizations, and lower transfusion burden when used consistently with monitoring.
edges.summary: Hydroxyurea is one of the most established disease-modifying therapies in sickle cell disease. Cochrane synthesis, the adult Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea, and the BABY HUG infant trial all point in the same direction: hydroxyurea meaningfully reduces acute complications and improves overall clinical course in appropriately selected patients.
edges.caveats: Benefits depend on adherence, dose titration, genotype, and safety monitoring for myelosuppression. The edge is strongest for HbSS and HbSbeta0 thalassemia and for acute clinical outcomes such as pain crises, acute chest syndrome, transfusions, and hospitalization rather than cure-level disease reversal.
